input.title: ZM3D playable: brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable: brief for PlayableX
Harmony Games, Zombie Match 3D. Prepared by Julia Lawson, 1 October 2025.

Start date
PlayableX start the build on Monday 3 November 2025. The kickoff call is the same day, 9:00 to 9:30 am Pacific. Work is paused until then while we look at a possible change to the core game.

This brief describes the game as it plays today. If the core game changes before November, we will go back over the affected sections with you at kickoff. The items, zombies, files and sound below stay the same either way.

1. Scenario and purpose
We picked your Scenario 1, a playable built on the core game.
What it's for: it should show the real game simply and honestly. Players who would not enjoy Zombie Match 3D should drop out at the ad, not after they install. We are optimising for retention and clean test results, not just the cheapest install.
How it plays: unlike the Domino Delights playable, this one does not run on rails. The player picks any items they like from the board and keeps making matches for as long as they can.

2. How a level plays
- The board is a physics pile of 3D items. The player drags items into a 7-slot tray.
- Any 3 matching items in the tray clear out and fire at the zombie at the front. The rocket launcher (our "Cannon" asset) fires them, using its projectile.
- Different items hit differently. For example, Grenade is powerful, Couch does splash damage, and the plushie is weak but funny. Showing this is part of the point.
- If all 7 tray slots fill without a match, that is a blunder. The tray clears, the surviving zombies enrage, and play goes on. A full tray is a penalty, not a loss.
- Zombies walk toward the player's base and damage it when they reach it.
Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
Lose: the zombies reach the base and the player's HP runs out. This is the only way to lose.
Reference: Brian recorded a reference level on 23 Sep and shared the video and assets in our channel on 24 Sep. It uses the same background, rocket launcher and win/lose rules. Its board (Grenade in red and green, Couch, Couch and Pillow, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick) was a mix for that recording. The board set in section 3 replaces it.

3. Board items
The default board is these eight items:
1. Grenade
2. Couch
3. Plushie Chick (the one you called "the duck")
4. Shuriken
5. Cute Axe
6. Gift Box
7. Cactus Plant
8. Dynamite
Every other board item on our pack list is an extra. Please make the board editable so we can swap extras in and change how many items are on the board. The hand-off sheet lists every item, marks each one Default or Extra, and shows its status.

4. Zombies and animation
Four zombies, one animation:
- Zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player
- Animation: walk
All four are in the Unity package we sent on 26 Sep (zombies_Characters_UnityPack.zip). Please re-rig only these four in Spine and carry over only the walk cycle. We may add more zombies later if size allows. Having control over the number of zombies would help us.

5. Sound
We only hand over sound that we own. Sound from a library or a bought pack stays with us until we have made our own version.
- You can use: matching sound, success sound, failure sound. These are ready.
- Background music: a new track made by us for the ad (not the in-game track). It is still being cut down to a loop and will follow.
- Rocket sound and explosion sound: the current ones come from a library and a bought pack, so we cannot send them. We will send our own versions when they are made. Until then, please don't use the in-game rocket or explosion sounds.
Music start: as you told us on the Domino Delights playable, music may only start after the player's first tap. Please keep that rule here.

6. Formats
As you asked:
- 3D: .fbx (binary, not ASCII), .glb or .blend
- 2D: .png (for 2D animation, character parts separated into pieces)
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

7. What is still coming from us
The hand-off sheet has one row per line of our pack list. Each row shows whether you already have the file (Delivered), whether it is exported and waiting in our outgoing folder (Ready), or whether we still owe it (Owed). For Owed rows it says what is owed and who has it. Items you already have but that changed afterwards (for example new colour versions) are marked Owed and will be sent again.

input.message:
Done. The brief and the hand-off list are both in my Drive, shared view-only with you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake.

Where the pack stands (96 lines on Brian's list):
• *Delivered: 8* (Couch, Couch and Pillow, Grenade, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick, Cannon, Background, Zombie characters)
• *Ready: 56*
• *Owed: 32*

What's behind the Owed count:
• Brian, 19 lines. 12 are Living Room/Kitchen items he saved out of Unity on Thu 25 Sep; Marcus said on the 26th those came out as ASCII FBX, so they need redoing as binary. The other 7 are 5 FBX he hasn't exported yet plus the item icons and UI PNGs from Figma.
• Claire, 9 lines. 6 FBX she hasn't sent yet. The other 3 are Chainsaw, Cone and Cactus Plant, which have new colour versions since the 25 Sep export, so they go again. Cactus is one of the 8 on the default board.
• Calvin, 3 lines. Background music is still being cut to a loop. Rocket and explosion sounds come from the Soundly library and a bought pack, so we hold them until he makes our own.
• Martin, 1 line: the .ttf fonts.

Of the default 8, Grenade, Couch and Chick are Delivered, Shuriken, Cute Axe, Gift Box and Dynamite are Ready, and Cactus is Owed. The brief uses Robert's 8 items and his 4 zombies (Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player) on the walk animation. I've moved the 32 Owed tickets under DES-313 to Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it.
Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fca677f88285489e783c400/edit
Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1otlfwv8h0d0f8ld1EdBANalvG3wIOiGDEGAACamuuKk/edit

Hi PlayableX team. Here are two documents to work from before the 3 November start:
• *Brief*, what to build from: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fca677f88285489e783c400/edit
It covers Scenario 1, the 8 default board items (every other item is a swappable extra), the 4 zombies and the one animation (Party Girl, Plumber, Magician and Football Player, walk only), the win and lose rules, the 7-slot tray, what sound you can use, and music starting only after the first tap.
• *Hand-off list*, one row per asset: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1otlfwv8h0d0f8ld1EdBANalvG3wIOiGDEGAACamuuKk/edit
Each row is marked Delivered, Ready (exported and waiting to send) or Owed. Owed rows say what's still coming and who has it.
The brief covers the game as it plays today. If the core gameplay changes, we'll go through those parts with you at kickoff. Both files are also shared with your intake address.
